result.summary: The environment is highly car-centric, characterized by wide expanses of asphalt and proximity to a highway interchange. Pedestrian infrastructure is minimal, with long unprotected crossing distances and a lack of marked crosswalks or signals in the immediate vicinity.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island or marked path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the wide asphalt area

hazards.name: High-Speed Geometry
hazards.description: The wide turning radii and proximity to highway ramps encourage high vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side slip lane and background highway approach

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Priority
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals are visible to manage interactions between people and vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian paths.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a raised island in the center of the wide roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the curb at the corners to reduce crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection featuring a large paved pedestrian island or plaza in the foreground. While the environment provides ample space for pedestrians, the expansive roadway widths and lack of prominent crossing signals suggest a design that prioritizes vehicle throughput.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the asphalt roadway in the foreground requires pedestrians to spend significant time exposed to traffic.

hazards.name: Wide curb radius

interventions.title: Curb Extensions

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to increase visibility of pedestrian crossing zones.

result.summary: The image shows a high-speed, multi-lane arterial roadway that is extremely hostile to pedestrians. There is a complete absence of sidewalks, crosswalks, or any form of pedestrian separation from heavy vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Facilities
hazards.description: There are no sidewalks or designated walking areas, forcing any pedestrian to walk directly in or immediately adjacent to high-speed traffic lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire foreground and midground along the roadway edges

hazards.name: High-Speed Multi-Lane Traffic
hazards.description: The roadway features at least five lanes of traffic with geometry that encourages high speeds, creating a lethal environment for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image across the full width of the asphalt

hazards.name: Extreme Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway without any refuge islands or marked crossings makes it impossible for a pedestrian to cross safely.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct wide, ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the roadway to provide physical separation for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes to slow traffic and decrease the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Protected Pedestrian Crossings
interventions.description: Install signalized mid-block or intersection crossings with high-visibility markings and pedestrian refuge islands.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is extremely hostile, characterized by a vast multi-lane asphalt roadway with no visible sidewalks, crosswalks, or safety infrastructure.
